lessons.title: Cripto e dinheiro digital
lessons.summary: O que é e o que não é.

cards.title: O que é o Bitcoin

events.l: ETFs à vista aprovados nos EUA

cards.text: O Bitcoin, lançado em 2009 pelo pseudônimo Satoshi Nakamoto, é uma moeda digital sem banco central. Um livro-razão público e compartilhado, a blockchain, registra todas as transações.

deep.x: Bitcoin is a digital currency that works without a central bank or company. A network of computers maintains a public ledger of all transactions, the blockchain.
Satoshi Nakamoto
Bitcoin's creator used the pseudonym Satoshi Nakamoto and disappeared from public view around 2011. Their identity remains unknown.
Key features
The pizza
On 22 May 2010, programmer Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 bitcoins for two pizzas, the first known real-world purchase. At 2025 prices, those bitcoins would be worth over a billion dollars.
Why it appeared then
The first block contained a newspaper headline about bank bailouts from January 2009, suggesting a response to the financial crisis.
Bitcoin's innovation was solving how strangers can agree on a ledger without trusting a central party.

cards.title: A blockchain
cards.text: Uma blockchain é uma cadeia de blocos de transações, cada um ligado ao anterior por criptografia. Alterar um bloco antigo exigiria refazer todo o trabalho que veio depois dele.

deep.x: A blockchain is a chain of blocks, each containing transactions and a cryptographic fingerprint (hash) of the previous block. Changing any old block breaks every link after it.

steps: Tampering with block 1 breaks the chain

deep.x: Why it's hard to cheat
To change a past transaction, an attacker would need to redo the work for that block and all later blocks, faster than the rest of the network combined.
Hashes
Beyond Bitcoin
Limits

x: Public blockchains are slow and costly compared with databases
Many "blockchain" projects didn't need one
Data on the chain is only as good as what's entered

deep.r: it only proves data hasn't changed since being recorded, not that it was correct

cards.title: Mineração
cards.text: Os "mineradores" de Bitcoin competem para resolver um quebra-cabeça matemático; o vencedor adiciona o próximo bloco e ganha bitcoins novos. Essa prova de trabalho consome muita eletricidade.

deep.x: Bitcoin miners compete to add the next block by solving a puzzle: finding a number that makes the block's hash meet a target. It takes enormous computing effort; checking a solution is instant.
Proof of work
The work makes attacks expensive: to rewrite history, you'd need more computing power than the rest of the network.
Energy use
Bitcoin mining uses electricity on the scale of a mid-sized country, roughly 100–200 TWh a year by Cambridge University estimates.
Proof of stake
Ethereum switched from proof of work to proof of stake in September 2022, cutting its energy use by over 99.9%.
Difficulty
The network adjusts difficulty about every two weeks so that blocks arrive roughly every ten minutes, however many miners join.
Mining turns electricity into security for the ledger.

cards.title: Oferta limitada
cards.text: Só vão existir 21 milhões de bitcoins. A recompensa da mineração cai pela metade a cada quatro anos, mais ou menos: o "halving".

deep.x: Bitcoin's rules cap total supply at 21 million coins. New coins enter through mining rewards, which halve about every four years.
Halvings
Scarcity argument
Supporters compare Bitcoin to digital gold: scarce, so it can't be inflated away. Critics note scarcity alone doesn't create value; demand does.
Lost coins
Millions of bitcoins are believed lost forever through forgotten passwords and discarded hard drives, making the effective supply smaller.
Satoshi's estimated holdings, around a million bitcoins, have never moved.

cards.title: Volatilidade
cards.text: Os preços das criptos oscilam loucamente. O Bitcoin já caiu mais de 70% várias vezes. Isso faz dele uma péssima reserva de valor de curto prazo para dinheiro de que você vai precisar.

deep.x: Crypto prices swing far more than shares or currencies. Bitcoin has fallen by more than 70% from a peak several times.
Why so volatile

items: No cash flows to anchor value

deep.x: What it means

x: Poor for money you need soon
Unsuitable as an emergency fund
Leverage can wipe out positions in hours

deep.x: Recoveries
Bitcoin has repeatedly recovered to new highs after crashes, passing $100,000 for the first time in December 2024. Past recoveries don't guarantee future ones; many other coins never recovered.
Only hold crypto money you could watch fall 80% without needing to sell.

cards.title: Stablecoins
cards.text: Stablecoins são tokens cripto feitos para acompanhar uma moeda como o dólar, geralmente lastreados em reservas. Algumas quebraram quando o lastro falhou.

deep.x: Stablecoins are crypto tokens designed to hold a steady value, usually one US dollar. Most are backed by reserves of cash and short-term government bonds.

items: kept stable by code and incentives

deep.x: Uses

items: Savings in dollars in high-inflation countries

deep.x: TerraUSD's collapse
In May 2022, the algorithmic stablecoin TerraUSD lost its dollar peg and collapsed with its sister token Luna, wiping out around $40 billion in value within days.
Even backed coins wobble
USDC briefly fell to about 87 cents in March 2023 when it emerged part of its reserves were held at Silicon Valley Bank.
Regulation
EU MiCA rules require stablecoin issuers to be authorised, hold reserves and allow redemption at par. The US passed its GENIUS Act for stablecoins in 2025.

deep.w: A stablecoin is as safe as a bank deposit
deep.r: it's only as safe as its reserves and issuer, with no deposit guarantee

cards.title: Cripto e crime
cards.text: Cripto é popular entre golpistas: plataformas de investimento falsas, golpes românticos do tipo "pig butchering" e falsos endossos de famosos. As transações são difíceis de reverter.

deep.x: Crypto's speed, global reach and irreversibility make it attractive to scammers. Most crypto losses for ordinary people come from fraud, not price falls.
Pig butchering

Scammers build a relationship over weeks via messaging or dating apps, then introduce a "profitable" crypto platform. Victims see fake gains, invest more, and can't withdraw. The name refers to fattening a pig before slaughter.
Fake celebrity ads
Ads using deepfaked or misappropriated images of celebrities and journalists to promote crypto schemes are widespread on social media.
Warning signs

x: Guaranteed or very high returns
Pressure to act quickly
Requests to move conversations to private apps
Withdrawal fees demanded before releasing funds

deep.x: Legitimate investments don't come through strangers in your messages.

cards.title: Sem chaves, sem cripto
cards.text: Se uma plataforma guarda suas criptos, você depende de ela continuar solvente e honesta. Quando a FTX quebrou em 2022, os clientes perderam acesso a bilhões.

deep.x: "Not your keys, not your coins": if an exchange holds your crypto, you depend on its honesty and solvency. If it fails, your coins may be gone.
FTX

In November 2022, FTX, one of the largest exchanges, collapsed after it emerged customer funds had been used by its sister trading firm. Founder Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted of fraud in 2023 and sentenced to 25 years.
Earlier failures
Self-custody risks

x: Lost seed phrase means permanent loss
Scams targeting wallet keys
No one to call for help

deep.x: Whoever controls the keys controls the coins.

cards.title: Regulação
cards.text: O regulamento MiCA da UE, aplicado a partir de 2024–25, define regras para prestadores de serviços cripto e stablecoins, incluindo licenças e proteção ao consumidor.

deep.x: Crypto regulation is catching up. The EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation (MiCA) creates a single rulebook for crypto service providers and stablecoins.
What MiCA requires
Taxes in Portugal
Since 2023, gains on crypto held for less than 365 days are taxed at 28% (or can be added to other income). Gains on crypto held longer are generally exempt.
Travel rule
EU rules require crypto providers to collect information on senders and recipients of transfers, like bank transfers, to fight money laundering.
Regulators

x: Banco de Portugal registers crypto providers for anti-money laundering
CMVM supervises under MiCA

deep.x: Regulation reduces some risks but doesn't make crypto prices less volatile.

cards.title: Se for experimentar
cards.text: Uma regra prática comum: invista só o que você poderia perder por inteiro, use plataformas reguladas, ative a autenticação em dois fatores e ignore retornos "garantidos". Não é recomendação.

deep.x: If you decide to buy crypto, a few basic rules reduce the risk of losing everything to scams, hacks or panic. This is general information, not personal advice.
Practical safeguards

items.b: strong unique password and authenticator app
consider hardware wallet for larger sums

deep.x: Behaviour

x: Decide in advance how much and why
Avoid leverage and trading on margin
Don't chase coins after big price jumps
Never share seed phrases or remote access to your device

deep.x: Position sizing
Treat crypto as a speculative extra, never as your safety net.

quiz.q: Qual é o número máximo de bitcoins?
O que é uma stablecoin?
options: Um token feito para acompanhar uma moeda

lessons.title: Finanças comportamentais
lessons.summary: Por que gente inteligente erra com dinheiro.

cards.title: Viés do presente
cards.text: Supervalorizamos recompensas agora em vez de depois. A maioria prefere €100 hoje a €110 na semana que vem, mas prefere €110 daqui a 53 semanas a €100 daqui a 52. A espera é a mesma.

deep.x: Present bias is our tendency to give too much weight to rewards now compared with rewards later. It explains why saving, dieting and studying are hard: costs are immediate, benefits distant.
Why it's inconsistent
In both choices, waiting one week earns €10. A perfectly consistent person would choose the same way. Economists call this pattern "hyperbolic discounting".
Where it shows up
Strategies

x: Commitment devices: lock money into savings or pensions
Automatic transfers that happen before you can spend
Make future rewards vivid: name savings pots after goals
Remove instant temptations: delete saved card details

deep.x: Make decisions for your future self in advance, when the present isn't shouting.

cards.title: Contabilidade mental
cards.text: Tratamos o dinheiro em "potes" mentais separados. Alguém pode deixar a poupança rendendo 2% enquanto carrega um saldo no cartão a 18%, perdendo dinheiro na diferença.

deep.x: Mental accounting means treating money as belonging to separate "pots" with different rules. It can lead to choices that cost real money.
The cost

x: Pay 18% on €3,000 of card debt = €540 a year
Earn 2% on €3,000 savings = €60 a year
Net loss: €480 a year

deep.x: Using the savings to clear the card would save €480 a year, then rebuild savings with the money no longer going to interest.
Why people do it

x: Savings feel "untouchable", even for a better use
Fear of having no buffer
Different accounts, different mental labels

deep.x: When pots help
Money is fungible: look at the whole picture, not each pot separately.

cards.title: Aversão à perda nos investimentos
cards.text: Os investidores odeiam tanto perder que seguram ações no prejuízo por tempo demais, esperando empatar, e vendem as vencedoras cedo demais: o efeito disposição.

deep.x: Losses feel roughly twice as painful as equal gains feel good. In investing, this leads to the "disposition effect": selling winners too early and holding losers too long.

items: sell quickly to lock in gain

deep.x: The evidence

Studies of brokerage accounts, notably by economist Terrance Odean in 1998, found investors were much more likely to sell shares that had risen than ones that had fallen, and that the losers they kept did worse than the winners they sold.
Why it hurts
Better questions

x: Would I buy this share today at this price?
Is the reason I bought it still valid?
Am I anchored to the price I paid?

items.w: "I'll sell when it gets back to what I paid"
items.r: "The price I paid is irrelevant to what happens next"

deep.x: The market doesn't know or care what you paid.

cards.title: Efeito manada
cards.text: Quando todo mundo está comprando, entrar parece seguro; quando todo mundo está vendendo, o pânico se espalha. Bolhas e quebras são, em parte, comportamento de manada.

deep.x: Herding is following what others do, assuming they know something. In markets, it amplifies booms and crashes.
Why we herd

x: Social proof: if everyone's doing it, it feels safe
Fear of missing out (FOMO)
Career risk: fund managers prefer being wrong together to wrong alone
Information cascades: people copy rather than research

deep.x: Examples
Buffett's advice
Warren Buffett famously advises being "fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful".
Social media and trading apps can accelerate herding, as in the 2021 GameStop surge driven by online forums.

cards.title: Excesso de confiança e trading
cards.text: Os investidores que mais negociam tendem a ganhar menos, sobretudo por causa dos custos e do mau timing. Um estudo famoso mostrou que os traders mais ativos ficavam vários pontos atrás por ano.

deep.x: Most people believe they're above-average investors. Overconfidence leads to frequent trading, which typically lowers returns through costs and poor timing.
The study

Economists Brad Barber and Terrance Odean analysed over 66,000 US households' brokerage accounts. Their 2000 paper, "Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth", found the most active fifth of traders earned 11.4% a year, against 17.9% for the market.
Why trading hurts
Gender differences
A follow-up study found men traded 45% more than women and reduced their returns more as a result, consistent with greater overconfidence.
For most investors, doing less is doing better.

cards.title: Viés de recência
cards.text: Achamos que as tendências recentes vão continuar: depois de um ano bom, todo mundo entra; depois de uma quebra, todo mundo foge, muitas vezes na pior hora.

deep.x: Recency bias makes us assume recent trends will continue. After strong years, investors pile in; after crashes, they flee, often at exactly the wrong moments.
The behaviour gap
Morningstar's annual "Mind the Gap" studies find that investors' actual returns lag the returns of the funds they own, by about one percentage point a year, because of badly timed buying and selling.
Examples

x: Heavy buying of tech funds in early 2000, just before the crash
Massive selling in March 2020, just before a rapid rebound
Crypto buying near the 2021 peak

deep.x: Countermeasures
Last year's winner is not a forecast.

cards.title: O efeito dotação
cards.text: Damos mais valor às coisas depois que elas são nossas. Canecas dadas a estudantes "valiam" para eles cerca do dobro do que para quem foi convidado a comprá-las.

deep.x: We value things more once we own them. That makes us reluctant to sell or switch, even when we should.

v.unit: median value of a mug, $ (Kahneman, Knetsch, Thaler 1990)

deep.x: The experiment
Students randomly given a university mug asked for more than twice as much to sell it as other students were willing to pay to buy it. Ownership alone changed its value.
Money examples
The status quo
The endowment effect links to status quo bias: we stick with what we have. Companies exploit it with free trials, since cancelling feels like losing something.

items.w: "I'll keep it because it's mine"
items.r: "Would I buy this today at its market price?"

deep.x: Judge what you own as if you were deciding to buy it today.

cards.title: Nudges
cards.text: Pequenas mudanças na forma de apresentar as escolhas podem ajudar: a adesão automática à previdência e planos do tipo "poupe mais amanhã" aumentam a poupança sem obrigar ninguém.

deep.x: A nudge changes how choices are presented without restricting them. Well-designed nudges help people act in their own long-term interest.
Automatic enrolment
A classic 2001 study by Brigitte Madrian and Dennis Shea found that automatic enrolment in a US company's pension plan raised participation among new employees from about 37% to 86%.
Save More Tomorrow

items.b: savings rates roughly quadrupled in the first study

deep.x: The concept
Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein popularised nudges in their 2008 book "Nudge". Many governments set up "nudge units" to apply the ideas.
Ethics

x: Nudges should be transparent and easy to opt out of
"Sludge" is the opposite: friction that makes good choices harder, like complicated cancellations

deep.x: Design defaults so the easy choice is the good one.

cards.title: Dinheiro e felicidade
cards.text: Renda maior está ligada a mais felicidade, e alguns estudos mostram que o ganho continua em rendas mais altas. Gastar com experiências, com os outros e para ganhar tempo tende a trazer mais alegria.

deep.x: Does money buy happiness? Research says yes, up to a point, and much depends on how you spend it.

items: Higher income linked to life satisfaction

deep.x: The debate

A famous 2010 study by Daniel Kahneman and Angus Deaton suggested day-to-day emotional wellbeing plateaued around $75,000 a year. Later research by Matthew Killingsworth found it kept rising. A joint 2023 study concluded happiness generally keeps rising with income, except for the least happy people, whose wellbeing plateaus.
How to spend

items.b: paying to avoid chores frees time
planning trips brings joy before them

deep.x: Security matters
Financial worries are a major source of stress. An emergency fund and low debt often do more for wellbeing than extra spending.
In experiments by Elizabeth Dunn and colleagues, people given money to spend on others reported more happiness than those told to spend it on themselves.

cards.title: Automatize as boas escolhas
cards.text: Programe transferências automáticas no dia do pagamento para a poupança e os investimentos. Você não gasta o que não vê, e evita a batalha da força de vontade.

deep.x: Automation makes good financial behaviour the default. You rely on a system, not daily willpower.
What to automate
Why it works

x: No decision fatigue
Money moves before you can spend it
Consistency beats occasional big efforts
Euro-cost averaging smooths market ups and downs

deep.x: Review, don't micromanage
Set it up once, review it once a year, and let it run.

quiz.q: Segurar ações no prejuízo por tempo demais, esperando empatar, se chama…
Quanto quem negocia com frequência costuma ganhar em comparação com o investidor paciente?
A adesão automática à previdência é um exemplo de…

cards.title: A mania das tulipas
cards.text: Na Holanda dos anos 1630, bulbos raros de tulipa teriam sido vendidos pelo preço de uma casa, antes de os preços despencarem em 1637. Hoje os historiadores acham que a mania foi menor do que diz a lenda.

deep.x: Tulip mania in the Dutch Republic in the 1630s is often called the first speculative bubble. Rare bulbs reportedly changed hands for extraordinary prices before the market collapsed in February 1637.
The legend
Charles Mackay's 1841 book "Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds" told of single bulbs exchanged for houses and of economic ruin across Holland.
The revision

Historian Anne Goldgar's 2007 research found the mania involved a relatively small group of wealthy merchants and craftsmen, and caused little wider economic damage. Many stories of ruin were moralising pamphlets.
Why bulbs?
The prized streaked patterns were later found to be caused by a virus, making them unpredictable and scarce.
Even the most famous bubble story was partly a bubble of exaggeration.

cards.title: A Bolha dos Mares do Sul
cards.text: Em 1720, as ações da britânica Companhia dos Mares do Sul dispararam e despencaram. Isaac Newton perdeu uma fortuna e teria dito que conseguia calcular o movimento das estrelas, mas não a loucura das pessoas.

deep.x: In 1720, shares in Britain's South Sea Company, which took over government debt in exchange for trading rights, soared and then collapsed within months.
What happened

x: The company promised profits from trade with South America that never materialised
It encouraged buying with loans and instalments
Many other "bubble companies" floated, including one "for carrying on an undertaking of great advantage, but nobody to know what it is"

deep.x: Newton's loss

Isaac Newton reportedly sold early at a profit, then bought back near the top and lost around £20,000, a fortune at the time. The quote about calculating the motions of heavenly bodies but not the madness of people is attributed to him but not well documented.
Consequences
France's Mississippi Bubble, run by John Law, collapsed the same year.

cards.title: A quebra de 1929
cards.text: A bolsa americana quebrou em outubro de 1929, ajudando a desencadear a Grande Depressão. Falências de bancos e erros de política econômica a aprofundaram.

deep.x: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 ended a speculative boom and helped trigger the Great Depression, the worst economic downturn of the industrialised world.
The fall
The Dow fell about 89% from peak to trough and didn't regain its 1929 peak until 1954.
Why it became a depression

x: Thousands of US banks failed, wiping out savings
The Federal Reserve let the money supply contract
Tariffs (Smoot-Hawley, 1930) hurt world trade
The gold standard spread deflation internationally

deep.x: Human cost
US unemployment reached about 25% in 1933.
Lessons applied

items.b: now act as lenders of last resort

deep.x: The crash was severe; policy mistakes turned it into a depression.

cards.title: Hiperinflação
cards.text: Quando os governos imprimem dinheiro para cobrir dívidas, os preços podem explodir. Na Alemanha em 1923, os preços dobravam a cada poucos dias; no Zimbábue em 2008, mais rápido ainda.

deep.x: Hyperinflation is extremely rapid inflation, often defined as prices rising more than 50% a month. It usually happens when governments print money to pay debts they can't otherwise finance.
Weimar Germany
In November 1923, one US dollar was worth about 4.2 trillion marks. Workers were paid twice a day and rushed to spend wages before prices rose again. Banknotes were used as wallpaper and kindling.
Hungary 1946
The worst recorded hyperinflation: at its peak, prices doubled roughly every 15 hours. The pengő was replaced by the forint.
How it ends
Zimbabwe
Hyperinflation's memory shaped Germany's strong preference for price stability, influencing the design of the ECB.

cards.title: Bretton Woods
cards.text: Em 1944, as grandes economias atrelaram suas moedas ao dólar, e o dólar ao ouro. Em 1971, os EUA acabaram com a conversibilidade em ouro, dando início às moedas flutuantes de hoje.

deep.x: In July 1944, delegates from 44 Allied countries met at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, to design the post-war monetary system.
How it worked

steps: Dollar convertible to gold at $35 an ounce

deep.x: Why it ended
On 15 August 1971, President Nixon suspended convertibility: the "Nixon shock".

x: US spending on the Vietnam War and social programmes
Dollars abroad far exceeded US gold reserves
Other countries began converting dollars into gold

deep.x: Legacy
Bretton Woods built institutions that still shape global finance.

cards.title: A bolha das ponto-com
cards.text: No fim dos anos 1990, empresas de internet sem lucro dispararam. O Nasdaq caiu quase 80% de 2000 a 2002. Algumas sobreviventes viraram gigantes.

deep.x: In the late 1990s, enthusiasm for the internet drove technology shares to extreme valuations, often for companies with little revenue and no profit.
The boom

x: New investors buying shares online
Companies valued on "eyeballs" and growth, not profits
Huge IPOs on their first day of trading

deep.x: The crash
The Nasdaq fell about 78% from its March 2000 peak to October 2002 and didn't regain the peak until 2015.
Survivors and failures
Amazon's share price fell more than 90% during the crash before becoming one of the world's most valuable companies.
A real technological revolution can still come with a financial bubble.

cards.title: A crise de 2008
cards.text: Financiamentos imobiliários arriscados nos EUA foram empacotados em títulos complexos. Quando os preços dos imóveis caíram, as perdas se espalharam pelo mundo. O Lehman Brothers quebrou em setembro de 2008.

deep.x: The global financial crisis began in US housing and spread through the financial system worldwide, causing the deepest recession since the 1930s.
Key events
Why it spread

x: Mortgages were repackaged into complex securities sold worldwide
Credit ratings overstated their safety
Banks were highly leveraged and dependent on short-term funding
Nobody knew who held the losses, so banks stopped trusting each other

deep.x: Aftermath
Lehman Brothers' bankruptcy, with over $600 billion in assets, remains the largest in US history.

cards.title: O resgate de Portugal
cards.text: Em 2011, durante a crise da dívida do euro, Portugal recebeu um resgate de €78 bilhões da UE e do FMI, com duras condições de austeridade. Saiu do programa em 2014.

deep.x: During the euro debt crisis, Portugal lost access to affordable market borrowing and requested international assistance in April 2011.
The troika

The €78 billion came from the EU's rescue funds (EFSM and EFSF) and the IMF, about two-thirds European and one-third IMF. Conditions were monitored by the "troika": the European Commission, the ECB and the IMF.
Conditions
Costs
Recovery
Portugal exited the programme in 2014 without a precautionary credit line. Growth, tourism and exports recovered, and public debt fell from around 130% of GDP in the mid-2010s to under 100% by 2024.
The bailout years shaped a generation of Portuguese and a cautious approach to public finances.

cards.title: O euro
cards.text: O euro foi lançado em 1999 para os bancos e em 2002 em cédulas e moedas. Portugal trocou os escudos a 200,482 escudos por euro.

deep.x: The euro launched on 1 January 1999 as an accounting currency for 11 countries, including Portugal. Notes and coins followed on 1 January 2002.
Benefits

x: No exchange costs or currency risk within the euro area
Easy price comparison across countries
Lower interest rates for countries like Portugal

deep.x: Challenges

items: Germany and Portugal may need different rates

deep.x: Without their own currencies, countries can't devalue to regain competitiveness, which made the debt crisis harder.
Portuguese coins
Each country designs the national side of its coins. Portugal's feature royal seals and the castles and shields of the national arms.
Many Portuguese still mentally convert large prices into "contos" (1,000 escudos) decades after the switch.

cards.title: Lições das crises
cards.text: As crises seguem padrões: crédito barato, preços subindo, histórias de "desta vez é diferente" e depois uma virada repentina. Diversificação e humildade protegem você.

deep.x: Financial crises differ in details but share recurring patterns. Recognising them helps protect your money.
Common ingredients
"This time is different"
Economists Carmen Reinhart and Kenneth Rogoff's 2009 book of that title documented eight centuries of financial crises and found the same belief before almost every one.
Personal protection

x: Diversify across assets and countries
Avoid heavy borrowing to invest
Keep an emergency fund
Be sceptical when everyone's sure prices can only rise
Hold investments you understand

deep.x: Humility and diversification have survived every crisis.

quiz.q: Quantos escudos valia um euro?
O que desencadeou a crise financeira de 2008?
options: Financiamentos imobiliários arriscados empacotados em títulos

cards.title: Receita, custos, lucro
cards.text: Receita é o dinheiro que entra com as vendas. Subtraia os custos e você tem o lucro. Uma empresa pode ter uma receita enorme e mesmo assim perder dinheiro.

deep.x: Every business comes down to this: money in (revenue) minus money out (costs) equals profit. Big revenue doesn't guarantee profit.
Layers of profit

items: Net profit: after interest and tax

deep.x: Big but unprofitable

Many fast-growing companies have large revenues but lose money for years while investing in growth. Uber, for example, didn't post a full-year operating profit until 2023, 14 years after it was founded.
Profit vs cash

x: Profit is an accounting measure
Cash is what's in the bank
They can differ hugely due to timing

deep.x: Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, cash is reality, as the saying goes.

cards.title: Margem bruta e líquida
cards.text: A margem bruta é o que sobra depois do custo direto das mercadorias. A margem líquida é o que sobra depois de tudo, incluindo salários, aluguel, juros e impostos.

deep.x: Margins show what share of each euro of sales a business keeps. Gross margin covers direct costs; net margin covers everything.
Typical margins
Example: a café
What margins reveal

x: Low-margin businesses need high volume
High-margin businesses attract competitors
Falling margins can signal price pressure or rising costs

deep.x: A business with thin margins has little room for mistakes.

cards.title: Custos fixos e variáveis
cards.text: Os custos fixos, como o aluguel, são os mesmos não importa quanto você venda; os variáveis, como os ingredientes, sobem a cada venda. Vender mais dilui os custos fixos.

deep.x: Costs behave differently as sales change. Fixed costs stay the same whatever you sell; variable costs rise with each unit.
Operating leverage
A business with high fixed costs and low variable costs, like a software company or airline, sees profits swing sharply with sales: great when sales grow, painful when they fall.
Example
Semi-variable costs

x: Energy: partly fixed, partly usage
Staff: fixed contracts plus overtime

deep.x: Every sale above break-even goes mostly to profit when fixed costs are high.

cards.title: Ponto de equilíbrio

viz.f: equilíbrio = custos fixos ÷ margem por unidade

cards.text: O ponto de equilíbrio é onde a receita cobre todos os custos. Um café com €6,000 de custos fixos por mês e €2 de lucro por cafezinho precisa vender 3,000 cafés por mês.

deep.x: The break-even point is where total revenue equals total costs. Below it, you lose money; above it, you make a profit.

v.f: Break-even units = fixed costs / contribution per unit

deep.x: The café example

x: Fixed costs €6,000 a month
÷ €2 contribution per coffee
= 3,000 coffees a month, about 100 a day

deep.x: Reducing break-even
Safety margin
The margin of safety is how far sales can fall before you hit break-even. A café selling 4,000 coffees has a margin of 1,000 coffees, or 25%.
Know your break-even before you open the doors.

cards.title: Fluxo de caixa
cards.text: Lucro não é caixa. Uma empresa pode ser lucrativa no papel, mas ficar sem caixa se os clientes pagarem atrasado. Muitas pequenas empresas quebram por esse motivo.

deep.x: Profit isn't cash. A business can show profits on paper but run out of money if customers pay late, stock piles up or loans fall due.
Working capital

items.b: time between paying and getting paid

deep.x: Late payments

Late payment is a major problem for small firms in southern Europe. The EU's Late Payment Directive sets 60-day limits for most business-to-business payments and 30 days for public authorities, but enforcement varies.
Managing cash

x: Invoice promptly and chase overdue payments
Negotiate supplier terms
Keep a cash buffer
Forecast cash weekly

deep.x: Businesses don't fail from lack of profit; they fail from lack of cash.

cards.title: Modelos de negócio
cards.text: As empresas ganham de jeitos diferentes: vendendo produtos, assinaturas, publicidade, comissões ou licenciamento.

deep.x: A business model describes how a company creates value and gets paid for it. The same product can be sold in very different ways.

items.b: others pay to use your IP

deep.x: Freemium
Free basic service, paid premium features. Works when a small share of paying users covers costs for everyone.
Subscriptions
Platforms
Platforms like app stores or ride-hailing apps connect two groups (buyers and sellers) and take a cut. They benefit from network effects.
Gillette's "razor and blades" model, selling the handle cheaply and profiting from replacement blades, is copied by printers and ink cartridges.

cards.title: Economias de escala
cards.text: Empresas maiores conseguem produzir cada unidade mais barato: compras em grande volume, máquinas especializadas e custos fixos diluídos.

deep.x: Larger producers can make each unit more cheaply. Fixed costs are spread over more units, and size brings purchasing power and specialisation.
Sources
Diseconomies of scale

x: Bureaucracy and slow decisions
Coordination problems
Loss of motivation and accountability

deep.x: Examples
Supermarket chains negotiate lower prices from suppliers; chip factories costing tens of billions of euros only make sense at enormous volumes.
Scale lowers costs, up to the point where complexity starts raising them.

cards.title: Fossos competitivos
cards.text: Warren Buffett procura "fossos": vantagens que protegem os lucros, como marcas, efeitos de rede, patentes ou custos de troca.

deep.x: Warren Buffett popularised the idea of an economic "moat": a durable advantage that protects a company's profits from competitors, like a moat around a castle.
Examples

items.b: people pay more for a trusted name
a platform is more valuable with more users
changing bank or software is a hassle
scale or location others can't match

deep.x: Moats erode

x: Technology shifts: digital cameras and Kodak
Regulation changes
New business models

deep.x: Why investors care
High profits attract competitors. Only companies with moats can sustain high returns for long.
A great business isn't just profitable; it's hard to copy.

cards.title: Valuation

viz.f: P/L = preço da ação ÷ lucro por ação

cards.text: O valor de mercado de uma empresa é o preço da ação vezes o número de ações. O índice preço/lucro (P/L) compara o preço com o lucro por ação.

deep.x: Investors estimate what a company is worth to decide whether its shares are cheap or expensive. Several simple measures help.

v.f: Market cap = share price × number of shares

deep.x: Price-to-earnings

v.f: P/E = share price / earnings per share

deep.x: A P/E of 20 means investors pay €20 for each €1 of yearly profit.
Typical P/E ranges
Other measures
High vs low P/E

x: High P/E: investors expect fast growth, or the shares are overpriced
Low P/E: slow growth expected, or the shares are underpriced

deep.x: A company's value is the cash it will generate in the future, discounted to today.

cards.title: Uma barraca de limonada
cards.text: Copos e limões custam €0,40 por copo; você vende a €1,50. A barraca custa €33 por dia. Você empata com 30 copos; o copo 31 já é lucro.

deep.x: A simple example brings all the concepts together: costs, margins and break-even.
The numbers
Break-even

x: €33 fixed costs
÷ €1.10 per glass
= 30 glasses

deep.x: A good day

x: 45 glasses × €1.10 = €49.50 contribution
− €33 fixed costs
= €16.50 profit

deep.x: Improving the stand

x: Raise the price to €2: break-even falls to 21 glasses
Cheaper lemons in bulk: higher contribution
Sell cookies too: more revenue from the same fixed costs

deep.x: Every business, from a lemonade stand to a multinational, follows the same arithmetic.

quiz.q: Um café tem €6,000 de custos fixos e ganha €2 por cafezinho. O ponto de equilíbrio é…
Por que uma empresa lucrativa pode ficar sem caixa?
options: Os clientes pagam atrasado enquanto as contas vencem

lessons.title: Seguros e risco
lessons.summary: Pagar pouco para evitar um desastre.

cards.title: Dividir o risco
cards.text: O seguro junta os pequenos pagamentos de muita gente para cobrir os poucos que sofrem grandes perdas. Cada um paga um prêmio previsível em vez de arriscar a ruína.

deep.x: Insurance works by pooling: many people pay predictable premiums so the few who suffer big losses can be compensated. Each person swaps an uncertain, possibly ruinous loss for a known cost.
The law of large numbers
With many policyholders, the total number of claims becomes predictable, even though each individual's fate isn't.
History

events.l: Great Fire of London spurs fire insurance

deep.x: Why it costs more than expected losses
You pay a bit more than your expected loss to avoid a loss you couldn't survive.

cards.title: Segure o que é grande
cards.text: O seguro vale mais para perdas que você não conseguiria absorver: sua casa, responsabilidade civil, saúde, renda. Para perdas pequenas, guardar dinheiro você mesmo costuma sair mais barato.

deep.x: Insurance is most valuable for losses you couldn't absorb from savings. For small losses, paying yourself is often cheaper over time.
Why small insurance is poor value
Extended warranties and gadget insurance often have high margins for the seller. The expected payout is much lower than the premium.
Self-insure

steps: Put the premiums into an emergency fund

deep.x: Priorities

items: Life if others depend on you

deep.x: Insure against catastrophe, not inconvenience.

cards.title: Prêmios e franquias
cards.text: O prêmio é o que você paga regularmente. A franquia é o que você paga antes de o seguro entrar em ação. Uma franquia maior costuma significar um prêmio menor.

deep.x: The premium is what you pay for cover. The deductible, franquia in Portugal, is the part of each claim you pay yourself. Choosing a higher deductible usually lowers the premium.
Example
If you rarely claim, policy B saves €100 a year.
Choosing

x: Pick a deductible you could pay comfortably from savings
Higher deductibles suit people with emergency funds
Consider how often you've claimed in the past

deep.x: Other terms
Use your emergency fund to self-insure small losses and pay less for insurance.

cards.title: Seguros obrigatórios

items: Incêndio do prédio: exigido em condomínios
Financiamento: vida e multirrisco geralmente exigidos

cards.text: Em Portugal, o seguro de responsabilidade civil do carro é obrigatório. O seguro contra incêndio é exigido para prédios em propriedade horizontal (condomínios), e os bancos o exigem nos financiamentos imobiliários.

deep.x: Some insurance is required by law in Portugal, because uninsured losses would hurt others.
Car insurance

cards.title: O truque da urgência

cards.title: Golpes de investimento

cards.text: Em Portugal, a CMVM, o Banco de Portugal e a ASF publicam listas de entidades não autorizadas. Se a empresa não estiver registrada, não invista.

cards.title: Golpes românticos

Commodity prices are global; their effects land in every shopping basket.

cards.title: Juros pelo mundo
cards.text: Quando o Federal Reserve dos EUA ou o BCE sobe os juros, pegar dinheiro emprestado fica mais caro no mundo todo, afetando moedas, financiamentos e mercados.

deep.x: Interest rates set by the big central banks ripple across the world through currencies, capital flows and borrowing costs.

steps: Dollar debts costlier for other countries

deep.x: The dollar's role
Much world trade and debt is priced in US dollars, so US rate changes affect everyone. A strong dollar makes oil and dollar debts more expensive in other currencies.
ECB and Portugal
Central banks around the world raised rates quickly to fight inflation, ending over a decade of very low rates.
When big central banks move, the whole world feels it.

cards.title: Mercados emergentes
cards.text: Economias de crescimento rápido, como Índia, Indonésia e Brasil, são uma parcela crescente da produção mundial. A China se tornou a maior economia do mundo por paridade de poder de compra por volta de 2016.

deep.x: Emerging markets are economies growing rapidly toward higher income, like China, India, Brazil and Indonesia. Their share of world output has risen strongly.

v.unit: share of world GDP by PPP, % (approx., 2024)

deep.x: Purchasing power parity
PPP adjusts for price levels: a euro buys more in India than in Portugal. By PPP, China's economy became larger than the US's in the mid-2010s; at market exchange rates, the US remains larger.
Opportunities and risks
India's rise
India became the world's most populous country in 2023 and has been one of the fastest-growing major economies.
The centre of the world economy is shifting east and south.

cards.title: Remessas
cards.text: Os migrantes mandam dinheiro para casa: as remessas para países de renda baixa e média passam de US$ 650 bilhões por ano, mais do que a ajuda externa.

deep.x: Remittances are money that migrants send home to family. For many countries, they're a vital source of income, larger than foreign aid.

v.unit: flows to low- and middle-income countries, $ billions (approx., 2023)

deep.x: Biggest recipients
India receives the most, over $120 billion a year.
Portugal's history
In the 1960s and 70s, remittances from Portuguese emigrants in France, Germany and elsewhere were a major source of foreign income. Emigrants still send billions of euros home each year.
Costs
The average cost of sending money internationally is around 6% of the amount, double the UN's 3% target. Digital transfer services have pushed costs down.
In some countries, like Tajikistan and Nepal, remittances equal a quarter or more of GDP.

quiz.q: O que é uma tarifa?
quiz.explain: Ela aumenta os preços para os consumidores.

quiz.q: Desde quando existe o mercado único da UE?
quiz.explain: Livre circulação de bens, serviços, pessoas e capitais.

cards.title: Saiba quanto você vale no mercado
cards.text: Pesquise a remuneração típica para o seu cargo, experiência e região em sites de vagas, pesquisas do setor e com colegas. Na negociação, dados vencem impressões.

deep.x: Knowing what others in similar roles earn is your strongest negotiating tool. Data replaces guesswork and nerves.
Where to look in Portugal

x: Recruiter salary guides published each year
Job listings that state ranges, increasingly common
Glassdoor and similar sites for larger employers
The EU Pay Transparency Directive, due by June 2026, requires employers to share pay ranges with candidates

deep.x: Factors that change value

items.b: Lisbon pays more than most regions

deep.x: Build a range
Negotiate from evidence: "the market rate is X" beats "I feel I deserve more".

cards.title: BATNA
cards.text: Sua BATNA é a melhor alternativa a um acordo negociado: o que você vai fazer se este acordo não sair. Quanto mais forte ela for, mais forte é a sua posição.

deep.x: BATNA stands for "best alternative to a negotiated agreement", a term from Roger Fisher and William Ury's 1981 book "Getting to Yes". It's what you'll do if this deal falls through.
Why it matters
Your BATNA sets your walk-away point. The better your alternative, the more confidently you can negotiate and the less you'll accept a bad deal.
Improving it
The other side's BATNA
Think about their alternatives too: how hard is it for them to find someone like you? A long, costly search strengthens your position.
The best way to get a better offer is to have another one.

cards.title: Ancoragem na negociação
cards.text: O primeiro número tende a ancorar a conversa. Se você tem bons dados, dizer primeiro um número ambicioso, mas justificado, pode jogar a seu favor.

deep.x: The first number mentioned tends to anchor the negotiation: later offers cluster around it. Research suggests first offers often predict final outcomes.
When to go first

x: If you have good market data, an ambitious but justified first number can pull the result up
If you lack information, let them go first and learn their range

deep.x: Justify the anchor

items.r: "Based on market data and my experience in X, €2,800 reflects the role"

deep.x: Counter-anchoring
If they anchor low, don't negotiate from their number. Restate your own range with evidence.
Ranges
Giving a range can work, but the other side will usually focus on the bottom. Make the bottom of your range a number you'd be happy with.
A study by Adam Galinsky and Thomas Mussweiler found that making the first offer often led to better outcomes for the party who made it.

cards.title: Pacote total
cards.text: Salário não é tudo: bônus, vale-refeição, plano de saúde, trabalho remoto, verba para treinamento e férias, tudo isso tem valor.

deep.x: Salary is only part of what a job is worth. Benefits, flexibility and growth can add substantial value.
Portuguese specifics

items.b: tax-free up to a daily limit

deep.x: The 14 payments include holiday pay and Christmas pay; the meal allowance limit is higher when paid on a meal card.
Valuing benefits

x: Health insurance can be worth hundreds or thousands of euros a year
Remote work saves commuting time and costs
Training budgets build future earnings

deep.x: When salary is fixed
Compare whole packages, in annual net terms.

cards.title: Negocie o aumento
cards.text: Os melhores momentos para pedir são depois de um grande sucesso, nas avaliações de desempenho ou ao assumir novas responsabilidades. Leve provas do seu impacto.

deep.x: Raises are easier to win with timing and evidence. Asking without preparation often ends with a vague "maybe later".
Good timing
Evidence

x: Results with numbers: revenue, savings, time, quality
New skills and certifications
Responsibilities beyond your role
Market data for similar roles

deep.x: If the answer is no

items.b: what would I need to achieve for a raise?

deep.x: Keep a "brag file" of achievements all year, so your evidence is ready.

cards.title: Ouça mais
cards.text: Pergunte do que o outro lado precisa: limites de orçamento, prazos, prioridades. Soluções criativas muitas vezes agradam os dois, como uma data de início mais tarde em troca de um salário maior.

deep.x: Good negotiators ask questions and listen. Understanding the other side's needs reveals solutions that work for both.
Questions to ask
Creative trades

x: Higher salary with a later start date
Lower base with a signing bonus
Title change now, raise in six months
More remote days instead of more pay

deep.x: Interests vs positions
"Getting to Yes" distinguishes positions (what people say they want) from interests (why they want it). Solving interests often unlocks agreement.
The more you know about their constraints, the better you can design a deal they can say yes to.

cards.title: O silêncio é poderoso
cards.text: Depois de fazer ou receber uma oferta, faça uma pausa. As pessoas costumam preencher o silêncio com concessões.

deep.x: After making or receiving an offer, a pause can be one of your strongest tools. People often fill silence with concessions or more information.
Why it works
Silence feels uncomfortable, so people rush to fill it, often by softening their position or explaining their flexibility.
Using it

x: After stating your number, stop talking
When you receive an offer, take a moment before replying
It's fine to say "let me think about it" and respond the next day

deep.x: Avoid

items.w: Instantly accepting the first offer
items.r: "Thank you, I'd like to take a day to consider it"

deep.x: Accepting too quickly can even leave the other side wondering if they offered too much.

cards.title: Bruto vs líquido
cards.text: Em Portugal, a diferença entre o salário bruto e o líquido inclui a Segurança Social (11% para os empregados) e a retenção do IRS. Compare as ofertas em valores líquidos.

deep.x: In Portugal, the gap between gross and net pay comes from social security contributions (11% for employees) and income tax withholding (IRS). Always compare offers in net terms.
Annual view
Most Portuguese salaries are paid 14 times a year, so compare annual gross, and the net that results.

x: = €28,000 a year gross

deep.x: Factors affecting net
Simulators
Online salary simulators use the official withholding tables to estimate net pay. Withholding is an advance; your final tax is settled in the annual IRS return.
A €200 higher gross isn't €200 more in your pocket.

cards.title: O custo de não negociar
cards.text: Uma diferença de €2,000 no salário inicial, composta pelos aumentos ao longo da carreira, pode somar dezenas de milhares de euros.

deep.x: A small difference in starting salary compounds over a career, because future raises are usually percentages of current pay.

v.unit: extra pay from €2,000 more a year, € thousands (2% yearly raises)

deep.x: Why it compounds

steps: Percentage raises on a bigger base
Higher future offers anchored on current pay

deep.x: Research
Studies of graduates suggest that those who negotiate starting offers often gain thousands of euros a year, and that many people, especially women in some studies, negotiate less often.
Low risk

x: Most employers expect some negotiation
A polite, evidence-based request rarely costs an offer
The worst common outcome is "no"

deep.x: A five-minute conversation can be worth tens of thousands over a career.

cards.title: Um roteiro
cards.text: "Estou animado com esta vaga. Com base na minha pesquisa e na minha experiência em X, eu esperava algo mais perto de €Y. Há alguma flexibilidade?"

deep.x: Having words ready reduces anxiety. A simple, positive script keeps the focus on the role and the evidence.
The script
"I'm excited about this role and the team. Based on my research and my experience in X, I was expecting something closer to €Y. Is there flexibility?"
Variations

items.a: If they say budget is fixed
items.b: "Could we look at a review in six months, or other parts of the package?"

items.a: If they ask your current salary
items.b: "I'm looking for a package in the range of €X to €Y for this role"

items.a: If you get a competing offer
items.b: "I'd prefer to join you, can you get closer to €Y?"

deep.x: Tone

x: Warm and collaborative, not confrontational
Confident, with numbers
Brief, then listen

deep.x: Rehearse your script out loud once; it makes the real conversation much easier.

quiz.q: O que é uma BATNA?
options: Sua melhor alternativa se o acordo não sair
quiz.explain: Uma BATNA forte dá poder de barganha.

quiz.q: O que você deve comparar entre ofertas de emprego?
options: O salário líquido e o pacote total

cards.title: Metas SMART
cards.text: Metas vagas ("poupar mais") raramente funcionam. Faça com que sejam específicas, mensuráveis, alcançáveis, relevantes e com prazo: "poupar €6,000 para um carro até dezembro de 2027".

deep.x: Vague goals like "save more" rarely work. SMART goals, a framework from management consultant George Doran in 1981, are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.
Example

items.w: "Save for a car"
items.r: "Save €6,000 for a car by December 2027: €250 a month"

deep.x: Break it down

x: €6,000 goal
÷ 24 months
= €250 a month

deep.x: Make it visible

x: Name a savings pot after the goal
Track progress monthly
Celebrate milestones

deep.x: A goal with a number and a date becomes a plan.

cards.title: Patrimônio líquido
cards.text: Seu patrimônio líquido é o que você tem menos o que você deve. Acompanhá-lo uma ou duas vezes por ano mostra se você está avançando.

deep.x: Net worth is what you own minus what you owe. It's the single best snapshot of your financial position.
Example
Tracking it

x: Update once or twice a year
Use realistic values, not hopes
Watch the trend, not the level

deep.x: Negative net worth
Many young people start with negative net worth due to student or car loans. That's normal; what matters is the direction.
Track net worth to see whether you're building wealth, not just earning income.

cards.title: Ordem de prioridades
cards.text: Uma sequência comum: monte uma pequena reserva, quite as dívidas caras, complete a reserva de emergência e depois poupe para suas metas e invista no longo prazo.

deep.x: With limited money, the order matters. A common sequence protects you first, then builds wealth.
Why this order

x: A small buffer prevents new debt when something breaks
Clearing 18% card debt is a guaranteed 18% return
A full emergency fund protects investments from forced sales
Then money can be invested for decades

deep.x: Exceptions

items.b: take it early, it's free money

deep.x: Build the foundation before the extensions.

cards.title: Horizontes de tempo
cards.text: O dinheiro de que você vai precisar em 2–3 anos deve ficar em lugares seguros. O dinheiro para 10+ anos aguenta os altos e baixos dos investimentos.

deep.x: When you'll need money decides where to keep it. Short-term money needs safety; long-term money can ride out swings.
Matching money to time
Why

items.b: losses much rarer for diversified portfolios

deep.x: Over one year, shares can fall sharply. Over 15+ years, history shows losses have been much rarer, though not impossible.
Glide path
As a goal approaches, shift gradually from shares to safer assets to lock in progress.
The closer the date, the safer the money should be.

cards.title: Caixinhas para gastos previstos
cards.text: Poupe todo mês para custos irregulares já conhecidos, como seguro do carro, férias ou Natal, para que eles não virem emergências.

deep.x: A sinking fund saves monthly for a known future expense. It turns big irregular bills into small regular ones.
Why they help

x: Irregular expenses stop being "emergencies"
No need to put them on credit cards
Your emergency fund stays intact for real surprises

deep.x: Common sinking funds
Setting up
Most "unexpected" bills are actually predictable.

cards.title: Taxa de poupança

viz.f: taxa de poupança = poupança ÷ renda líquida

cards.text: Sua taxa de poupança, a parcela da renda que você poupa, importa mais que o retorno dos investimentos no começo. Passar de 5% para 15% tem um efeito enorme com o tempo.

deep.x: Your savings rate is the share of income you save. Early in life, it matters far more than investment returns.

v.f: Savings rate = amount saved / net income

items.m: including investments and extra debt payments

deep.x: Why it's powerful
Example over 20 years
Two sides

x: A higher savings rate means more money invested
It also means you've learned to live on less, so you need less in retirement

deep.x: Raise your savings rate a little every year; you'll barely notice the difference in spending.

cards.title: Revise todo ano
cards.text: Uma vez por ano, revise renda, gastos, dívidas, seguros, investimentos e metas. A vida muda; seu plano também deve mudar.

deep.x: Life changes: jobs, relationships, children, homes. An annual money review keeps your plan aligned with your life.
Checklist
Good timing

x: January, for a fresh start
After your IRS return
After big life events

deep.x: Small fixes, big effects
Switching an insurer, cancelling forgotten subscriptions or moving savings to a better account can each save hundreds of euros a year.
One afternoon a year can be the most valuable money hours you spend.

cards.title: Casais e dinheiro
cards.text: Dinheiro é uma das maiores causas de briga. Conversem abertamente sobre metas e hábitos; muitos casais usam uma conta conjunta para os gastos comuns, mais contas pessoais.

deep.x: Money is one of the most common sources of conflict for couples. Talking openly early prevents bigger problems later.
Topics to discuss
Splitting costs

items.b: simple, can feel unfair with different incomes
each pays in line with income
full sharing, needs trust and agreement

deep.x: Regular check-ins
A monthly or quarterly "money date" to review the budget and goals keeps both partners informed.
In Portugal, the default marriage property regime is "comunhão de adquiridos": property acquired during the marriage is jointly owned, while what each owned before stays separate.

cards.title: Ensinando as crianças
cards.text: Mesada, cofrinhos e deixar as crianças cometerem pequenos erros ensinam a lidar com dinheiro desde cedo. Algumas pesquisas sugerem que os hábitos se formam até os 7 anos.

deep.x: Children learn money habits early. Research for the UK's Money Advice Service by the University of Cambridge suggested many money habits are formed by age seven.
By age

items.b: pocket money, saving for a toy

deep.x: Three jars
A third jar, share, introduces giving.
Let them make mistakes
Spending all their pocket money on something disappointing teaches more than a lecture, while the stakes are small.
Talk about money openly at home: silence teaches anxiety.

cards.title: Um plano de 1 página
cards.text: Em uma página: renda mensal, custos fixos, taxa de poupança, meta da reserva de emergência, dívidas com suas taxas e duas ou três metas com datas.

deep.x: A good financial plan fits on one page. Simplicity makes it easy to follow and update.
Example plan

items.b: €6,000 car fund by 2027, invest €100 a month for retirement

deep.x: Using it

x: Keep it somewhere visible
Update after big changes
Review every year

deep.x: A simple plan you follow beats a complex one you forget.

quiz.q: O que é patrimônio líquido?
Onde costuma ficar o dinheiro de que você vai precisar daqui a dois anos?
options: Depósitos seguros ou contas de poupança

cards.title: Para que servem os impostos
cards.text: Os impostos financiam os serviços públicos: saúde, escolas, estradas, aposentadorias e defesa. Em Portugal, impostos e contribuições sociais somam cerca de 35–38% do PIB.

deep.x: Taxes fund public services and transfers: healthcare, schools, roads, pensions, defence and more. In Portugal, taxes and social contributions together are about 35–36% of GDP.
Where the money goes
Comparison
The social contract

x: Taxes pay for services everyone uses
Social security provides insurance against old age, illness and unemployment
Progressive taxes redistribute from higher to lower incomes

deep.x: Taxes are the price of public services; the debate is about how much and how fairly.

cards.title: Diretos e indiretos
cards.text: Os impostos diretos incidem sobre renda e patrimônio, como o IRS. Os indiretos incidem sobre o consumo, como o IVA e os impostos sobre combustíveis, e são pagos por todos que compram.

deep.x: Taxes come in two main forms. Direct taxes are on income and wealth; indirect taxes are on spending.
Portugal's main taxes
Fairness
Indirect taxes take a larger share of income from lower earners, who spend more of what they earn. Direct taxes can be made progressive.
Balance
Portugal relies heavily on indirect taxes and social contributions compared with some EU countries.
Everyone pays tax, even those who earn too little to pay income tax, through IVA on purchases.

cards.title: Imposto de renda progressivo

items: Fatia do topo: alíquota mais alta

cards.text: O IRS é progressivo: as fatias mais altas da renda são tributadas com alíquotas maiores. Só a renda dentro de cada faixa paga a alíquota daquela faixa.

deep.x: Portugal's IRS is progressive: income is divided into brackets, and each slice is taxed at its bracket's rate. Rates rise from roughly 12–13% on the first slice to 48% on the highest.

items: Minimum: income below a threshold is protected

deep.x: How brackets work
Only the income inside each bracket pays that bracket's rate. Someone earning just over a threshold pays the higher rate only on the few euros above it.
Minimum existence
The "mínimo de existência" protects low incomes so that tax doesn't push take-home pay below a minimum level.
Solidarity surcharge
Very high incomes pay an additional solidarity surcharge on top of the highest rate.
Higher rates apply only to higher slices of income, never to all of it.

cards.title: Marginal vs média

items.w: "O aumento me jogou numa faixa mais alta, então ganho menos"
items.r: Só os euros a mais pagam mais imposto

cards.text: Passar para uma faixa mais alta nunca reduz o seu salário líquido total: só a renda extra é tributada pela alíquota maior. Sua alíquota média é sempre menor que a sua alíquota máxima.

deep.x: The marginal rate is the rate on your last euro of income. The average rate is total tax divided by total income. The average is always lower.

items.w: "A raise could push me into a higher bracket and I'd take home less"
items.r: Only the extra income is taxed at the higher rate

deep.x: Example (simplified brackets)
Why the myth persists
Monthly withholding tables used to cause small jumps in net pay at some thresholds, which fed the belief. Reforms smoothed the tables, and your final tax is calculated on the annual return anyway.
Benefits that end
The real "trap" can come from benefits or allowances that stop above certain incomes, not from the tax brackets themselves.
A raise always increases your take-home pay from income tax's point of view.

cards.title: Alíquotas do IVA
cards.text: O IVA de Portugal continental tem três alíquotas: 6% para itens essenciais, como alimentos básicos, 13% para alguns itens, como comida de restaurante, e 23% padrão. As ilhas têm alíquotas menores.

deep.x: IVA (value added tax) is charged on most goods and services. Mainland Portugal has three rates; the Azores and Madeira have lower ones.
What goes where

items.b: basic food, medicines, books, some energy
restaurant food, some wines and canned goods

deep.x: Islands
How IVA works

steps: Pays the difference to the state

deep.x: Temporary changes
Portugal temporarily applied 0% IVA to a basket of essential foods in 2023 to fight inflation.
IVA is collected by businesses but paid by consumers.

cards.title: E-fatura
cards.text: Pedir nota fiscal com o seu NIF permite que alguns gastos contem para deduções no IRS, como saúde, educação e moradia, e ajuda a combater a sonegação.

deep.x: E-fatura is the system where businesses report every invoice to the Tax Authority. Asking for invoices with your NIF lets some spending count toward IRS deductions.
Why it exists
IVA deduction on some services
Part of the IVA you pay at restaurants, hairdressers, car repair shops, vets and gyms can be deducted from your IRS, if you ask for an invoice with your NIF.
Checking

x: Check and classify invoices by late February each year
Invoices with mixed activities may need manual classification

deep.x: Portugal's monthly "Fatura da Sorte" lottery has rewarded people for asking for invoices with their NIF.

cards.title: Deduções
cards.text: As deduções reduzem o imposto devido: saúde, educação, aluguel e dependentes são categorias comuns, cada uma com limites.

deep.x: Deductions ("deduções à coleta") reduce the tax you owe after it's calculated. Each category has its own percentage and limit.
Main categories

items.b: 15% of rent paid, with a cap that has been rising

deep.x: Refund or bill
Most employees get a refund because monthly withholding exceeds the final tax. A big refund means you lent the state money interest-free during the year.
Tips

x: Ask for NIF on qualifying invoices
Check that rent receipts are issued electronically
Confirm dependants and household details

deep.x: Deductions reward keeping invoices; the system does most of the work if you ask for your NIF.

cards.title: IRS Jovem
cards.text: Portugal oferece imposto de renda reduzido para jovens nos primeiros anos de trabalho, pelo regime IRS Jovem. As regras já mudaram várias vezes; confira as condições atuais.

deep.x: IRS Jovem gives young people a partial income tax exemption in their first years of work. It aims to keep young talent in Portugal.
The 2025 version
The exemption is capped at an income limit and applies to those aged up to 35.
Changes over time

events.l: broadened to all young workers under 35, up to 10 years

deep.x: Check

x: Eligibility rules have changed several times
Withholding may already reflect it
Confirm in the annual IRS return

deep.x: Young workers should check they're receiving IRS Jovem; the savings can be significant.

cards.title: Autônomos
cards.text: Os trabalhadores autônomos emitem "recibos verdes", entregam declarações trimestrais à Segurança Social e podem usar um regime simplificado em que só parte da renda é tributada.

deep.x: Self-employed workers in Portugal ("trabalhadores independentes") issue electronic receipts, the "recibos verdes", and handle their own tax and social security.
Social security
Simplified regime
Under the simplified IRS regime, only part of income is taxed. For most professional services, 75% of income is considered taxable, unless expenses are proven.
IVA
Small self-employed workers with turnover below a threshold (€15,000 in 2025) can be exempt from charging IVA.
Plan ahead

steps: Set aside tax and social security

deep.x: Put aside around a quarter to a third of every receipt for tax and contributions.

cards.title: Sua declaração anual
cards.text: Toda primavera, confira o IRS pré-preenchido no Portal das Finanças. Confirme dependentes, deduções e rendimentos antes de enviar; o IRS automático serve para muita gente.

deep.x: Each year, residents submit an IRS return covering the previous year's income. Many use the pre-filled version or automatic IRS on the Portal das Finanças.
What to check
Automatic IRS
For simple situations, mainly employees and pensioners with no complex income, the Tax Authority proposes an automatic return. You just confirm it, or it's confirmed automatically at the deadline.
Joint or separate

items: can help when incomes differ a lot
often best when incomes are similar

deep.x: The portal can simulate both options.
Deadlines
The return period runs from 1 April to 30 June. Late submission can lead to fines.
Ten minutes checking your pre-filled return can avoid mistakes and missed refunds.

quiz.q: Num sistema progressivo, um aumento que leva você a uma faixa mais alta significa que…
options: só a renda extra é mais tributada
toda a renda é mais tributada
quiz.explain: As alíquotas marginais valem por faixa.

quiz.q: Qual é a alíquota padrão do IVA em Portugal continental?
